statement: The 2025 World Seniors Championship (officially the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship) was a snooker tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England.
The tournament was held at the Crucible Theatre for the seventh consecutive year.
The event was the 16th edition of the World Seniors Championship.
The World Seniors Championship was first held in 1991.
The event was open to amateur players over 40 and professional players who were over 45 and also ranked outside the top 64 in the snooker world rankings.
The event was organised by the World Seniors Tour.
The event was broadcast in the United Kingdom by Channel 5 and internationally by other broadcasters.
Igor Figueiredo was the defending champion, having defeated Ken Doherty 5‍–‍2 in the 2024 final.
Igor Figueiredo lost 2‍–‍4 to Wayne Townsend in the first round.
Alfie Burden held leads of 4‍–‍1 and 7‍–‍2 against Aaron Canavan in the final.
Alfie Burden won 8‍–‍4 against Aaron Canavan to claim his first World Seniors title.
The tournament produced five century breaks.
Four of the century breaks were compiled by Dominic Dale.
Dominic Dale made the highest break, a 131, in his semi-final match against Canavan.
The final of the event was Michaela Tabb's last appearance as a traditional snooker referee.
Michaela Tabb had a 24-year career as a traditional snooker referee.
Michaela Tabb had refereed two World Championship finals.
The tournament was sponsored by bookmaker JenningsBet.
Four referees officiated: Mark Beale, Michaela Tabb, Rod Eaton, and Proletina Velichkova.
Figueiredo, as the defending champion, was given the top seed.
Other seeded players were Doherty, Jimmy White, Tony Drago and Tony Knowles.
Jimmy White was a four-time winner of the event.
Joe Perry and Dominic Dale retired as professional players after their defeats in the qualifying stages of the 2025 World Championship.
Joe Perry and Dominic Dale's retirement made them eligible to compete in the World Seniors Championship.
Several players had to qualify for the event.
Aaron Canavan, Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene and Townsend qualified for the event during the so-called Race to the Crucible Series.
Aaron Canavan won the 2018 edition of the event.
Four players qualified through various continental Seniors Championships.
Craig Steadman won in Europe.
Hassan Kerde won in Asia-Pacific.
Charl Jonck won in Africa.
Fabio Luersen won in the Americas.
Alfie Burden defeated Andy Lavin, Rodney Goggins, Stuart Watson and Matthew Ford to win the Golden Ticket tournament.
The Golden Ticket tournament win qualified Alfie Burden for the final stages.
The winner of the event received £20,000.
The runner-up of the event earned £10,000.
The first round took place on 7 and 8 May.
Each match in the first round was played as the best of 7 frames.
Joe Perry made two breaks of 76 to take a 2‍–‍0 lead against Fabio Luersen.
Joe Perry compiled a 94 and a 59 to win 4‍–‍2 against Fabio Luersen.
Craig Steadman recovered from 0‍–‍2 against Dominic Dale to tie the scores.
Dale won the fifth frame against Steadman.
Dale compiled a century break of 107 in the sixth frame against Steadman.
Dale clinched a 4‍–‍2 victory against Steadman.
Wayne Townsend won the first frame of the match against Igor Figueiredo with a break of 53 and on the final black ball.
Figueiredo replied with a half-century of his own and then took the lead at 2‍–‍1 against Townsend.
Townsend won three frames on the spin, the last one again on the final black, to seal victory against Figueiredo.
Aaron Canavan manufactured breaks of 51, 89, 72 and 51 to defeat Andrew Norman 4‍–‍1.
Alfie Burden faced Jimmy White in the first round.
Burden won the first two frames against White.
White produced an 82 break in the third frame to halve the deficit against Burden.
Burden won the fourth frame on the re-spotted black against White.
Burden manufactured a 92 break in the fifth frame against White to advance into the quarter-finals.
Ken Doherty took a 2‍–‍0 lead against Charl Jonck.
Jonck went on to win four consecutive frames against Doherty, featuring breaks of 64 and 63, to win the match.
Tony Drago compiled a 75 break in the first frame of his duel with Gerard Greene.
The match between Drago and Greene went into a decider, which Drago won aided by a break of 68.
Hassan Kerde whitewashed Tony Knowles, making breaks of 53, 62, 66 and 59 in the process.
The quarter-finals took place on 9 May.
Each match in the quarter-finals was played as the best of 7 frames.
Dale compiled breaks of 97, 99 and 128 as he beat Perry 4‍–‍1.
In his match against Burden, Drago won the first frame and then took two consecutive frames on the re-spotted black to edge 3‍–‍0 in front.
Burden won four frames on the spin, featuring breaks of 53 and 51, to advance into the semi-finals after defeating Drago.
Kerde and Jonck shared the first four frames, but Kerde then took two, one of them with a break of 85, to win the match.
Canavan took a 3‍–‍1 lead against Townsend.
Townsend compiled an 85 break in the fifth frame against Canavan to halve the deficit.
Canavan went on to take the following frame and seal victory with a 4‍–‍2 result against Townsend.
The semi-finals took place on 10 May.
Both matches in the semi-finals were played as the best of 11 frames.
Burden produced breaks of 57 and 65 as he took a 4‍–‍0 lead against Kerde.
Kerde replied by winning two consecutive frames and halving the deficit against Burden.
Burden made a break of 97 to go 5‍–‍2 in front and won the following frame to clinch victory against Kerde.
Canavan and Dale shared the first four frames of their semi-final.
Dale then made back-to-back century breaks, of 109 and 131, and won another frame to go within one of victory at 5‍–‍2 against Canavan.
Canavan won four consecutive frames, including the decider, to book a place in the final after defeating Dale.
On 11 May, Burden and Canavan contested the best-of-15-frame final.
The final was divided into three mini-sessions of five frames each.
Both Burden and Canavan were competing in a World Seniors final for the second time.
Aaron Canavan won the World Seniors title in 2018.
Alfie Burden was runner-up in the World Seniors final in 2023.
The first five-frame mini-session was refereed by Michaela Tabb.
Michaela Tabb retired from traditional snooker refereeing after the tournament.
Canavan won the opening frame against Burden.
Burden then won four consecutive frames with breaks including 74 and 54 as he moved 4–1 ahead against Canavan.
Proletina Velichkova refereed the remainder of the final.
Canavan won the first frame of the second mini-session against Burden.
Burden took three consecutive frames against Canavan with breaks of 65, 109, and 80.
Canavan won the 8th frame to leave Burden leading 7–3.
The third and final mini-session lasted two frames.
Canavan won frame 11 against Burden.
Burden made a 76 break in the 12th frame to secure an 8–4 victory and win his first World Seniors title.
